parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **scarcity**?
choices: The human effort, physical and mental, used in the production of goods and services
Natural resources used in production, such as minerals, soil, forests and water
The situation where resources are limited/finite while wants are unlimited, so choices must be made
Man-made resources used to produce other goods and services, such as machinery or buildings

rows.answer:

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **production possibility curve (PPC)**?
choices: A curve showing the maximum combinations of two goods/services that can be produced when all resources are fully and efficiently used
The amount of one good that must be given up to produce more of the other good when moving along the curve
A combination of goods outside the curve which cannot be produced with the current resources and technology
Producing at a point on the PPC so it is not possible to produce more of one good without producing less of the other

rows.answer: A curve showing the maximum combinations of two goods/services that can be produced when all resources are fully and efficiently used.
rows.notes: Award 1 mark for a precise definition. Do not award the mark for an example alone.

parts.text: What is meant by the term **production possibility curve (PPC)**?

rows.answer: A curve showing the maximum combinations of two goods/services (1) that can be produced when all resources are fully and efficiently used (1).
rows.notes: Award 1 mark for the key idea of the definition and 1 mark for a valid developing point, which may be a relevant example such as the one shown. An example given without the key idea gains a maximum of 1 mark.

parts.text: Define the term **productive efficiency (on a PPC)**.

rows.answer: Producing at a point on the PPC so it is not possible to produce more of one good without producing less of the other.
rows.notes: Award 1 mark for a precise definition. Do not award the mark for an example alone.

parts.text: What is meant by the term **productive efficiency (on a PPC)**?

rows.answer: Producing at a point on the PPC (1) so it is not possible to produce more of one good without producing less of the other (1).
rows.notes: Award 1 mark for the key idea of the definition and 1 mark for a valid developing point, which may be a relevant example such as the one shown. An example given without the key idea gains a maximum of 1 mark.

parts.text: Define the term **an unattainable point on a PPC**.

rows.answer: A combination of goods outside the curve which cannot be produced with the current resources and technology.
rows.notes: Award 1 mark for a precise definition. Do not award the mark for an example alone.

parts.text: What is meant by the term **an unattainable point on a PPC**?

parts.text: Define the term **economic growth (shown on a PPC)**.

parts.text: Define the term **opportunity cost (on a PPC)**.

Describe how a rise in incomes might affect the demand for an inferior good.

rows.answer:
Award 1 mark for a relevant point and 1 mark for a linked development, for example:
- demand falls/curve shifts left (1) because consumers can now afford better-quality alternatives (1)
rows.notes: Only one point should be credited. A second, undeveloped point does not gain the development mark.

parts.text: Describe one way advertising can affect the demand for a product.

- advertising can build brand loyalty (1) so consumers keep buying even if rivals cut prices (1)

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **supply**?
choices: A rise in quantity supplied caused by a rise in the price of the product (movement up the supply curve)
A fall in quantity supplied caused by a fall in the price of the product (movement down the supply curve)
The amount of a product that firms are prepared to offer for sale at each price over a period of time
A tax on spending/goods and services which raises firms' costs and reduces supply

rows.answer:
Correct option: **C** (The amount of a product that firms are prepared to offer for sale at each price over a period of time)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of an extension in supply
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of a contraction in supply
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of an indirect tax

A: incorrect, that is the meaning of a contraction in supply

parts.text: Define the term **supply**.

rows.answer: The amount of a product that firms are prepared to offer for sale at each price over a period of time.

parts.text: What is meant by the term **supply**?

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **price elasticity of supply (PES)**?
choices: The responsiveness of quantity supplied to a change in price
When a change in price causes a proportionately smaller change in quantity supplied (PES less than 1)
When quantity supplied cannot change whatever the price (PES = 0)
When a firm is producing less than the maximum it could with its existing resources

rows.answer:
Correct option: **A** (The responsiveness of quantity supplied to a change in price)
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of price inelastic supply
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of perfectly inelastic supply
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of spare capacity

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **price elastic supply**?

parts.text:
Lumo Partners produces plastic packaging in Doha. Its factory currently uses only 58% of its capacity.

Explain why the supply of Lumo Partners's plastic packaging is likely to be price elastic.

rows.answer:
Award 1 mark for identifying a relevant point, 1 mark for developing it and 1 mark for applying it to the context.

Example:
- Lumo Partners has spare capacity (1) because 58% of capacity is used (1), so if the price of plastic packaging rises it can increase output quickly using idle machines and workers (1)
rows.notes: Accept any other valid explanation. Answers with no reference to the context cannot gain the third mark.

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **mixed economy**?
choices: The part of the economy owned and controlled by the government/state
A good that is under-consumed in a free market because people underestimate its benefits, such as education
An economy in which resources are allocated by both the private sector and the public/state sector
When people benefit from a good without paying for it, so firms cannot charge for it

rows.answer:
Correct option: **C** (An economy in which resources are allocated by both the private sector and the public/state sector)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of public sector
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of merit good
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of free-rider problem

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **private sector**?
choices: An economy where resources are allocated by the price mechanism with little or no government intervention
The part of the economy owned and controlled by the government/state
The part of the economy owned and controlled by individuals and private firms, mainly aiming for profit
A good that is under-consumed in a free market because people underestimate its benefits, such as education

rows.answer:
Correct option: **C** (The part of the economy owned and controlled by individuals and private firms, mainly aiming for profit)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of free market economy
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of public sector

parts.text: Evaluate whether the government of Lumera should pay for street lighting. Use the information above and your own knowledge of economics to support your answer.

grid.descriptor: No rewardable material.
Some relevant knowledge with limited or no application to the context. Reasoning is simple, often a list of points. Any judgement is asserted and unsupported.

Accurate knowledge applied to the context, with developed chains of reasoning, though the answer may lack balance. Evaluation considers alternative views and may reach a judgement, but the support for it is partial.

Accurate knowledge applied consistently, making effective use of the context and data. Chains of reasoning are well developed and balanced. Evaluation is sustained and reaches a clear, supported judgement, for example by weighing short-run against long-run effects or considering what the outcome depends on.

indicative: AO2/AO3: Street lighting is a public good: non-excludable and non-rival
AO2/AO3: Firms cannot charge users because of the free-rider problem, so they cannot make a profit
AO2/AO3: The market fails to provide it, so there is under-provision
AO2/AO3: Better lighting may reduce crime, giving benefits to the whole community
AO4: Government spending on lighting has an opportunity cost
AO4: It must be funded by taxes, which some residents may oppose
AO4: Local councils or community groups might provide it
AO4: Benefits may be smaller than expected if crime has other causes
AO4: A supported judgement, for example stating what the outcome depends on or which argument is stronger and why.

levels.ao_split: AO2 4 marks, AO3 4 marks, AO4 4 marks

intro: Towns in Valdoria have poor street lighting and local residents say crime has increased. Private firms have refused to install lighting because they say they cannot make a profit from it.

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **regulation**?
choices: A payment by the government to producers to reduce their costs and increase supply
A tax on spending on goods and services collected from firms, which raises costs and reduces supply
When the government directly supplies a good or service usually financed through taxation
Rules or laws set by the government to control the behaviour of firms or consumers

rows.answer:
Correct option: **D** (Rules or laws set by the government to control the behaviour of firms or consumers)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of subsidy
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of indirect tax
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of state provision

parts.text: An indirect tax on a product will shift
choices: the supply curve to the left
the supply curve to the right
the demand curve to the left
the demand curve to the right

rows.answer:
Correct option: **A** (the supply curve to the left)
B: incorrect
C: incorrect
D: incorrect

parts.text: A subsidy to producers is likely to result in
choices: a higher price and higher quantity
a higher price and lower quantity
a lower price and a higher quantity
no change in price

rows.answer:
Correct option: **C** (a lower price and a higher quantity)
A: incorrect
B: incorrect
D: incorrect

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **externality**?
choices: A cost or benefit to a third party not involved in the production or consumption of a good
The total benefit to society of an activity equal to private benefit plus external benefit
A financial penalty imposed on a firm or individual for breaking a rule or law
The cost of an activity paid by the individual or firm carrying it out

rows.answer:
Correct option: **A** (A cost or benefit to a third party not involved in the production or consumption of a good)
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of social benefit
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of fine
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of private cost

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **negative externality**?
choices: A financial penalty imposed on a firm or individual for breaking a rule or law
The total cost to society of an activity equal to private cost plus external cost
A cost to third parties from the production or consumption of a good, such as pollution
The cost of an activity paid by the individual or firm carrying it out

parts.text: Define the term **pollution permit**.

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **pollution permit**?
choices: A licence issued by the government that allows a firm to emit a fixed amount of pollution and which can often be traded with other firms
A money penalty imposed by the government when a firm or person breaks a rule, such as an emissions limit
Laws passed by the government that ban or restrict an activity, such as dumping waste in rivers
A tax on a product or activity that damages the environment so that its price reflects more of the external cost

rows.answer:
Correct option: **A** (A licence issued by the government that allows a firm to emit a fixed amount of pollution and which can often be traded with other firms)
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of fine
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of legislation
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of environmental tax

parts.text: A government wants firms to cut pollution while letting the cheapest polluters make the biggest cuts. The most suitable policy is
choices: a minimum wage
tradable pollution permits
a subsidy to polluting firms
a ban on all production

rows.answer:
Correct option: **B** (tradable pollution permits)
A: incorrect, this is a labour market policy
C: incorrect, this would encourage more production and pollution
D: incorrect, a ban stops useful output as well as pollution

parts.text: One disadvantage of fines as a way of reducing pollution is that
choices: they increase the supply of the product
they always raise large amounts of tax revenue
they reduce the cost of production
firms may simply pay them if the fine is small compared with their profit

rows.answer:
Correct option: **D** (firms may simply pay them if the fine is small compared with their profit)
A: incorrect
B: incorrect
C: incorrect

parts.text: A subsidy for solar panels is most likely to
choices: reduce the number of firms producing them
raise their price and reduce the quantity bought
lower their price and increase the quantity bought
shift the demand curve to the left

rows.answer:
Correct option: **C** (lower their price and increase the quantity bought)
A: incorrect
B: incorrect
D: incorrect

parts.text: Which one of the following is an example of a tax used to deal with an externality?

parts.text:
The government of Lumera fines factories L£32,000 each time they exceed their limit on waste released into rivers.

Explain one reason why fines may not stop all pollution in Lumera.

rows.answer:
Award 1 mark for identifying a relevant point, 1 mark for developing it and 1 mark for applying it to the context.

Example:
- Some factories may find it cheaper to pay the fine (1) because cutting waste needs costly new equipment (1), so if the L£32,000 fine is small compared with their profits, they may keep polluting (1)
rows.notes: Accept any other valid explanation. Answers with no reference to the context cannot gain the third mark.

rows.notes: Award 0 marks if both curves are shifted or the wrong curve is shifted. Accept curved or straight lines; labels such as D1/S1, P1 and Q1 or equivalent.
